channel.title: Degree Programs :: CS Two Year Refactor
channel.description: Three degree programs — Computer Science, Cybersecurity, and Artificial Intelligence — share the same two-year computational foundation before specializing entirely in the upper division. See Computing Foundations for that shared core, its design rationale, and the full course-by-course breakdown. Cybersecurity and Artificial Intelligence are not separate degrees built from scratch — each is the Computer Science degree with a curated choice of upper-division electives. A student completing either specialization earns both that specialization’s degree and a Bachelor of Computer Science, with no additional coursework or cost beyond what the Computer Science degree already requires. A student can instead forgo a named specialization and use that same elective flexibility to chart their own path toward the career they envision.

item.title: Computer Science
item.description: The department’s flagship degree, the Bachelor in Computer Science retains its flexibility as a degree option providing students with many electives. This flexibility allows students to customize the degree to the career they have chosen for themselves, mixing computing know-how from technical electives with other-discipline domain knowledge from unrestricted electives. Our specialization degrees – Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity – are essentially the computer science degree with specific electives chosen. Thus, every major graduating with a specialization degree also earns a Bachelor of Computer Science with no additional coursework required.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Proposed for Fall 2027, the Artificial Intelligence degree builds upon the department’s expertise and existing courses in AI, machine learning, and knowledge representation to present a cohesive synthesis of modern AI techniques and architectures. As a specialization degree, students earning a Bachelors in AI will also earn a Bachelors of Computer Science with no additional coursework required. The Bachelor of Artificial Intelligence will be reviewed by ABET for accreditation in our next cycle.

item.title: Cybersecurity
item.description: The Cybersecurity degree leverages the department’s expertise in cybersecurity and designation as a Center for Academic Excellence in Cybersecurity Research, providing hands-on training including systems-level thinking and secure coding practices. As a specialization degree, students earning a Bachelors in AI will also earn a Bachelors of Computer Science with no additional coursework required. The Bachelor of Cybersecurity is accredited by ABET.
